Evidence
7.

Submissions 8.
I have heard Sh.Mahender Kumar, ld. counsel for petitioner, Sh.G.S. Bisht, ld. counsel for respondent no.1 and 2 as well as Sh.Rajesh Goel, ld. counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company.
I have also gone through written submissions filed on behalf of petitioners.
Issue No.1 9
. It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken MACT No.1353/2016 Page 4 while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
10.

sentences.text: To prove the occurrence of accident in the manner as claimed in the claim petition, petitioners have examined eye witness PW2 Pawan Kumar Gupta who deposed that he is the eye witness of the accident and well conversant with the facts of the case.
PW2 deposed that on 18.04.2015 at about 9.00 p.m., he was returning from Bhopura for his home along with his brother Rajiv.

When he was crossing the road from DLF side, he saw a truck bearing no.UP-23H-9726 coming in a very rash and negligent manner from Ghaziabad side and took a turn towards Loni side, at that time a boy was coming on bicycle from other side and was going towards Ghaziabad side.
PW2 further says that he saw the driver of the said truck hitting the bicycle and the said boy fell down on the road and sustained multiple grievous injuries.
PW2 stated that name of said boy was Tausif.
PW2 further deposed that he immediately rushed to the spot of accident to help the boy and he informed the father of Tausif and also informed the police.
The injured was taken to GTB Hospital and during treatment Tausif died on 19.04.2015.
PW2 stated that said accident was caused due to sole rash and negligence of driver of offending truck.
PW2 further stated that he knew Tausif and his father Firoz Firoz Khan Etc vs Mukesh Kumar Etc on 14 December, 2023

11. During cross-examination PW2 stated that on 18.04.2015 he was going to his house from DLF flats near Bhopura and he was walking at the time of accident.
He stated that deceased was coming towards Ghaziabad from Delhi side and truck was going from Ghaziabad towards Delhi side.
PW2 further stated that he saw the truck while coming from Ghaziabad side.
He further stated that he knew Tausif as brother of Tausif was running a shop near to shop of PW2 where Tausif used to come and that is why he knew him.
12. Though eye witness PW2 was cross-examined but respondents have failed to put any dent to his testimony.

PW2 remained consistent that he saw the incidence of hitting the deceased by the offending truck from his own eyes and that the said truck hit the deceased while being driven in rash and negligent manner.

Even otherwise perusal of certified copy of FIR No.422/2015 of PS Sahibabad Ex.PW1/A shows that offending truck bearing registration no. UP-23H-9726 was involved in the accident in question in which deceased died.
Certified copy of charge sheet of criminal case Ex.PW1/C shows that respondent no.1/driver was charge sheeted by UP police for causing accident while driving offending vehicle no. UP-23H-9726.
Site plan of the place of accident is also on record.

13. Testimony of PW2 who is eye witness to the accident in question coupled with record of criminal case in the opinion of this Tribunal is sufficient to establish that deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of offending truck bearing registration no. UP-23H-9726 being driven by respondent no.1.

In view of testimony of PW2 coupled with criminal case record, this Tribunal finds that petitioners have established that vehicle no.UP-23H-9726 was in fact involved in the MACT No.1353/2016 Page 6 accident and evidence establish that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
Issue No.2 14. In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 15.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Tausif.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6

Decided on 31.10.2017,
laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.

The multiplier should be chosen from the said table MACT No.1353/2016 Page 8 with Firoz Khan Etc vs Mukesh Kumar Etc on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161000925/
5 reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation) The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.

sentences.text: Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.
The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

16. Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased :
17.
The petitioner no.1 Firoz Khan (PW1) in his evidence has deposed that deceased was aged about 18 years at the time of accident.
He proved certified copy of post mortem report of deceased as Ex.PW1/B in which age of deceased is mentioned as 18 years.
In the criminal case documents of FIR No.422/2015 also age of deceased is mentioned as 18 years.
As per these documents, age of deceased on the date of his death was 18 years.
These documents in the opinion of this Tribunal are conclusive proof of age of deceased.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of accident (18.04.2015) was 18 years.
MACT No.1353/2016 Page 9 Assessment of Income of deceased :

18. Petitioner no.1 (PW1) in his deposition stated that his deceased son was working as helper with Amit Tyre at Dilshad Garden and was getting a salary of Rs.9,200/-
per month but due to untimely demise of deceased, petitioners suffer huge economic loss.
He also deposed that deceased was elder son of the petitioner and was having responsibility of entire family especially of his younger brothers and sisters.

He proved copy of salary certificate of deceased as Ex.PW1/H.
19.

To prove the work and income of deceased, petitioners have also examined PW3 Sandeep Kumar who by way of his affidavit has deposed that he is proprietor of Amit Tyres dealing in tyres and wheel alignment at Shop No.22A, D-15/A-4, Dilshad Garden, New Delhi.

sentences.text: PW3 proved salary certificate of deceased issued to his father as Ex.PW1/H.
Perusal of document Ex.PW1/H shows that deceased Tausif s/o Feroz was working with firm namely Amit Tyres as a helper and was drawing salary of Rs.9,200/- per month.

20. Though PW3 was cross examined in which he stated that he has not issued any employment letter to deceased and has not filed any document showing he being proprietor of Amit Tyres, but as per pleadings of the claim petition deceased was working as a helper in a tyre and wheel alignment shop and it is quite common that such type of shops do not issue any employment letters to its workers that too engaged as helpers.
However in view of the certificate issued by PW3 which is Ex.PW1/H 21.

Having considered the evidence of PW1 as well as PW3 on the question of the income of the deceased, this Tribunal is of considered MACT No.1353/2016 Page 10 view that the factum of deceased drawing salary of Rs.9,200/- per month at the time of accident has been proved by preponderance of probabilities on the basis of Ex.PW1/H.
As such the income of the deceased is taken to be Rs.9,200/- per month.

Application of Multiplier:
22.
As held above, deceased was 18 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
In Para 21 of the judgment, the guidelines for the multiplier were laid down in accordance with age are as under:

MULTIPLIER AGE GROUP OF DECEASED  M-18 Age group between 15 to 20 & 21  to 25 years)
 M-17 Age group between 26 to 30 yrs  M-16 Age group between 31 to 35 yrs  M-15 Age group between 36 to 40 yrs  M-14 Age group between 41 to 45 yrs  M-13 Age group between 46 to 50 yrs  M-11 Age group between 51 to 55 yrs  M-9 Age group between 56 to 60 yrs  M-7 Age group between 61 to 65 yrs  M-5 Age group between 66 and above 23.
In view of the above, multiplier of 18 has to be applied against the age bracket of 15 to 20 years to determine the compensation.

sentences.text: This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the MACT No.1353/2016 Page 11 judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

25. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 18 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged below 40 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.

Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
26.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

sentences.text: Instant claim petition has been filed by two petitioners i.e. parents of deceased.
However it has come in the evidence of PW1 Firoz Khan that he was working with a firm namely Sardar Khan Motors and this fact has been proved by him by employment certificate Ex.PW1/G.
Thus, it cannot be said that petitioner no.1 Firoz Khan was dependent upon the deceased, however petitioner no.2 i.e. mother of deceased can be said to be dependent upon deceased.
Since it has been observed that the deceased was survived by one dependent, one-half of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.

NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
28.

In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-,
18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

Further, in MACT No.1353/2016 Page 13 view of recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @
Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, loss of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs.

INTEREST ON AWARD 31.
In this case one of the important aspect is regarding fixing the pendency interest rate on the amount of compensation.
Counsel for the MACT No.1353/2016 Page 14 insurance submits that pendente lite interest may not be awarded during the period from 23.08.2018 when ld.
Predecessor of this Tribunal returned the claim petition for want of territorial jurisdiction, till 16.03.2023 when Hon'ble High Court disposed off MAC Appeal No.967/2018.

32. Counsel for the petitioner on the other hand submits that petitioner is entitled for the pendente lite interest even for the above said period as there was no fault of the petitioner for delay in disposal of the matter.
33. Having considered the submissions and having gone through the record, generally petitioner is entitled for pendente lite interest for period during which claim petition remain pending.
Such interest can be withheld only in a situation where circumstance show that petitioner has consciously delayed the proceedings.
In this case earlier claim petition was returned by ld.
Predecessor of this Tribunal on wrong assumption of facts, vide judgment dated 23.08.2018, which was set aside by Hon'ble High Court by order dated 16.03.2023.
in such situation there is no fault attributable to petitioner, for earlier returning of claim petition and that finding having been set aside by Hon'ble High Court.
Therefore petitioners is entitled for interest @ 8% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
LIABILITY 34.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
It is matter of record that the vehicle in question was duly insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.
Therefore the amount of compensation is payable by respondent no.3/ insurance company to the petitioners.

opennyai_summary.issue:
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving vehicle bearing no.
Up-23H-9726 on 18.04.2015 at 9.00 pm in front of Bhopra Tiraha, Ghaziabad, U.P. in a high speed
and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against cyclist Tausif who fell down and sustained
injuries and succumbed to the injuries?
Opp (2)Whether the petitioner is entitled for any
compensation, if so and for what amount?
Opp (3)Relief.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
. It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken MACT No.1353/2016 Page 4 while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
10.
13. Testimony of PW2 who is eye witness to the accident in question coupled with record of criminal case in the opinion of this Tribunal is sufficient to establish that deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of offending truck bearing registration no. UP-23H-9726 being driven by respondent no.1.
In view of testimony of PW2 coupled with criminal case record, this Tribunal finds that petitioners have established that vehicle no.UP-23H-9726 was in fact involved in the MACT No.1353/2016 Page 6 accident and evidence establish that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 15.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6

Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
20. Though PW3 was cross examined in which he stated that he has not issued any employment letter to deceased and has not filed any document showing he being proprietor of Amit Tyres, but as per pleadings of the claim petition deceased was working as a helper in a tyre and wheel alignment shop and it is quite common that such type of shops do not issue any employment letters to its workers that too engaged as helpers.
However in view of the certificate issued by PW3 which is Ex.PW1/H 21.
Having considered the evidence of PW1 as well as PW3 on the question of the income of the deceased, this Tribunal is of considered MACT No.1353/2016 Page 10 view that the factum of deceased drawing salary of Rs.9,200/- per month at the time of accident has been proved by preponderance of probabilities on the basis of Ex.PW1/H.
As such the income of the deceased is taken to be Rs.9,200/- per month.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
25. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 18 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged below 40 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
 Deductions out of earning of the Number of  deceased dependents MACT No.1353/2016 Page 12  Where dependent is 1 Half  Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd  members is 2 to 3  Where the number of dependent family 1/4th  members is 4 to 6  Where the number of dependent family 1/5th  members exceeds 6 (six)

in such situation there is no fault attributable to petitioner, for earlier returning of claim petition and that finding having been set aside by Hon'ble High Court.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-,
18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.
Since, the deceased was survived by seven legal heirs, therefore,
the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,32,000/- (48,000 X 2 + 18,000 + 18,000) under this head.
